sentences.text: The claimants in MFA No.201320/2019 are seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at Vijayapur (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC No.442/2017, vide its judgment and award dated 30.03.2019.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at Vijayapur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The insurer is also in appeal in MFA No.201531/2019 challenging the liability fastened on it to pay the compensation determined in the above case.
2. The claimants are the husband and children of deceased Gurubai.

The claimants claimed that the NC: 2023:KHC-K:5558 deceased was proceeding in a tractor-trailer unit bearing registration No.KA-28/TB-3148 and KA-28/TB-3151 along with her goods from the house of a person named Gurubasappa Sajjan and that she suffered injuries when the tractor-trailer over turned due to rash and negligent driving by its driver.
The claimants claimed that the deceased suffered injuries and was shifted to Sanjeevini Hospital, Vijayapur where she died during the course of treatment.

They claimed that the deceased was a coolie and was earning a sum of Rs.10,000/- per month and due to her untimely death, they had lost the financial and emotional support of the deceased and therefore,
they filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation from the owner and insurer of the tractor-trailer.
3. The owner of the tractor-trailer denied the averments in the claim petition.
However, he contended that the tractor-trailer unit was insured and therefore, the insurer is liable to pay the compensation.
The insurer NC: 2023:KHC-K:5558 however contended that the deceased was a passenger travelling in the goods vehicle and therefore, the risk of her death was not covered under the policy of insurance.
It also contended that even if the goods were transported in the tractor-trailer, those goods do not belong to the deceased.

It contended that the driver of the tractor- trailer did not have a valid driving licence and hence, it denied its liability to indemnify the owner of the tractor- trailer.
4.
Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant No.1 was examined as PW.1 and he marked Exs.P1 to P10.

The insurer examined one of its officials as RW.1 and marked the policy of insurance as Ex.R1.
5.
Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident happened due to negligence on the part of the driver of the tractor-trailer.
It also held that the deceased suffered injuries and later succumbed to the injuries.

It considered the age of the NC: 2023:KHC-K:5558 deceased as 40 years and her notional income at a sum of Rs.7,000/- per month and after deducting 1/3rd of notional income towards her personal and living expenses, awarded the following compensation:

The Tribunal rejected the contention of the insurer that the deceased was a passenger travelling in a goods vehicle and directed the insurer of the tractor-trailer to pay the aforesaid compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realisation.
6.
Being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claimants are in appeal while the insurer has also challenged its liability to pay the compensation.

The learned counsel for the claimants contended that the deceased was aged 40 years and therefore, loss of future prospects ought to have been considered at the rate of 40% and he also submitted that the notional income ought to have been considered at a sum of Rs.10,250/- per month.
8.
Per contra, learned counsel for the insurer contended that the deceased was not a coolie but claimed that she was travelling along with her goods.
He contended that there was no reference to the goods carried in the tractor in the complaint at Ex.P2 and spot mahazar.
Therefore, he contended that it has to be held that the deceased was travelling as a passenger in the goods vehicle.
He therefore contended that the insurer is not liable to indemnify the owner against the risk of death of the deceased.
9. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the claimants and the learned counsel for the insurer.
The death of the deceased in the accident involving a tractor-trailer referred above cannot be disputed in view of the complaint lodged as per Ex.P2 and the spot panchanama at Ex.P5.
The fact that the deceased suffered injuries was proved by Exs.P8 to P10.
The only question that requires to consider is whether the deceased was travelling in the tractor-trailer along with her goods.
The claimants claimed that the deceased was travelling along with her goods in the tractor-trailer when the accident happened on 23.01.2017.
The insurer to avoid liability claimed that the deceased was a gratuitous passenger in a goods vehicle.
However, the insurer did nothing to establish it, except examining an interested witness of RW.1 who was not an eyewitness.

In that view of the matter, the finding of the Tribunal that the deceased was travelling in the tractor-trailer along with her goods Ningappa @ Ninganna And Ors vs Appanagouda And Anr on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69401892/
5 cannot be set aside on the basis of the contentions raised by the insurer.

sentences.text: Consequently, the finding that the accident happened due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the tractor-trailer and that the deceased was - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5558 travelling in the said vehicle along with her goods does not warrant any interference.

11. In so far as the quantum of compensation is concerned, as rightly contended by the learned counsel for the claimants, the Tribunal must have considered the notional income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.10,250/- per month.

The deceased was 40 years old, however, there was no document placed on record to indicate that she was exactly aged 40 years and therefore, 25% of her notional income deserves to be considered as loss of future prospects.

Consequently, the claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation which is re-determined as follows:-
 Particulars
Amount
Sl .No. (in Rs.)

1 Loss of dependency 15,37,560/-
 2 Loss of consortium 44,000/-
3 Loss of estate, funeral expenses 33,000/-
 etc.
 Total 16,14,560/-
12.
In view of the above, the appeal filed by the claimants in MFA No.201320/2019 is allowed in part.

The compensation of Rs.9,30,602/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.16,14,560/- which is payable by the insurer along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.

13. The enhanced compensation amount along with interest shall be deposited by the insurer before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this Judgment.
14. Upon deposit, 40% of the enhanced compensation and interest shall be deposited in the name of the claimant Nos.2 and 3 each in any nationalized Bank for a period of five years.

The remaining portion shall be released in favour of claimant No.1.
15.
The appeal filed by the insurer in MFA No.201531/2019 is dismissed.
